role: Calorimeter-performance expert (selection panel) — judging the energy-measurement case for the RADiCAL shower-max sampler, T10 Aug-2026 campaign
assessment:
VERDICT ON THE ENERGY CASE: as measured, this campaign demonstrates a timing-and-coarse-position layer operating at shower max inside a calorimeter stack; it does NOT yet demonstrate a calorimeter. Crucially, the published site does not pretend otherwise — the "Conclusions so far" card in /Users/jameswetzel/Dropbox/01_Research/HEP/RADiCAL/02_Analysis/2026-08_CERN_T10/RADiCAL_TB_T10_Aug-2026/index.html claims (1) hundred-ps shower timing, (2) a measured material trade between light-collection channels, (3) beam knowledge — no energy-resolution claim appears anywhere, and linearity is stated with its ±15% envelope caveat in the Materials section. The energy case is not overclaimed; it is simply not made.

What CAN legitimately be claimed on energy from this dataset: (a) Relative light-collection efficiency of the three capillary channels per shower GeV — DSB1/LuAG = 2.2x in ADC-eq/GeV (~1350 vs ~620), 3.5x in response-per-MIP — is robust because the W/LYSO tile stack and beam are identical and the comparison is ratio-based (index.html Materials table; units caveat correctly flags the soft absolute scale). This is a genuine, transferable measurement of the capillaries as light-collection channels. (b) Response is proportional to E above 3 GeV to within the ±15% cross-run gain envelope, and the high-energy behavior is consistent with a linear x Longo fixed-depth-sampling model (FINDINGS.md lines 468-497, SaturationStudy: residuals +3.2/0/+19.6/+14.5/-5.5% at 3/5/7/9/11 GeV are monotone in time-of-day, not energy; Longo migration expectation -3.2/-6.0/-8.5% at 7/9/11 GeV). (c) ONE intrinsic-resolution statement exists in the entire campaign: the erfc fit to the direct-hit ΣLG edge at 5 GeV gives edge width/position = 10.5% ± 1.6% as an UPPER bound at full response, explicitly still containing position falloff and the T10 momentum bite (FINDINGS.md lines 102-110). (d) Sub-linearity below 3 GeV, qualitatively as expected for fixed-depth sampling (line 322-323). Everything else measured as sigma/E is position-smearing dominated and characterizes the T10 beam-spot/module-size convolution, not the detector: 33.6 ± 1.4% at 5 GeV (run 15, line 227), 20.4 ± 1.1% at 7 GeV best (line 340), 31.9 ± 3.8% at 9 GeV daytime run (line 362). The log itself states the correct diagnosis: "A true energy resolution measurement needs impact-position tagging... not more events" and "the measurement is blocked by the beam-spot/position degeneracy, which a million events would not resolve" (lines 106-110, 123-127).

What CANNOT be claimed: any stochastic/constant/noise-term decomposition; any intrinsic sigma/E point (the 10.5% bound at 5 GeV has zero discrimination power for the FCC-ee question — 3%/sqrt(E) predicts 1.3% at 5 GeV and 20%/sqrt(E) predicts 8.9%, both comfortably under the bound); linearity at the per-mille-to-percent level FCC-ee physics requires (the ±15% envelope is ~two orders of magnitude away, and nothing in this dataset can be tightened retroactively because the MIP gain anchor was correctly struck down — FINDINGS.md lines 481-483); longitudinal containment or the event-by-event depth-fluctuation term of shower-max-only sampling (the Longo correction fixes the MEAN response, not the variance — the concept-defining question of whether shower-max stationarity keeps depth fluctuations second-order in the response was neither measured nor simulated-and-validated); absolute energy scale (ADC-eq is readout-relative; pe scale "possible and planned"); hadronic response (off-coincidence pions used only as MIP sets); e/pi separation beyond one tag-and-probe training point (90.9% eff / x3, or 73.4% / x19 with energy window, run 15 — FINDINGS.md lines 302-305); anything above 11 GeV, where the LG ceiling (~13.6k ADC-eq) already compresses the brightest channel (line 565-567: DSB1 at 11 GeV "additionally the LG ceiling").

Fit to targets: FCC-ee PF EM goals (3-15%/sqrt(E), sub-percent constant term, per-mille scale control, 45.6 GeV Z-pole showers) — this campaign provides no evidence for or against; the detector was never tested above one quarter of Z-pole energy and its readout saturated getting there. The credible FCC-ee story TODAY is a 5D/timing layer: DSB1 at 133 ± 5 ps at 9 GeV reference-included, intrinsic ~75 ps at 9 GeV pending the downstream-reference confirmation, trend constant term 79 ps with a mechanistic explanation (3x shorter scintillation tail) — extrapolating to few-tens-of-ps at Z energies if the constant term holds, which is competitive as an embedded timing/position element in someone else's calorimeter. Muon collider: the natural pitch (BIB rejection wants <60 ps EM timestamps + extreme radiation hardness, which is RADiCAL's stated raison d'etre) — but radiation hardness was not measured at all this campaign, so the muon-collider case currently rests entirely on prior/assumed material properties plus this timing result. Is it a calorimeter, a timing/position layer, or both? On this evidence: a timing/position layer, with the calorimeter question open — not disproven (the one bound and the Longo-consistent mean response are compatible with a useful ~10%/sqrt(E)-class device), but entirely undemonstrated.
strengths: Honest scope: index.html's conclusions card claims timing, material trade, and beam knowledge — no energy-resolution claim is made anywhere, and linearity carries its ±15% envelope caveat inline. The energy case is under-claimed, not over-claimed; this is the right scientific posture and the panel should credit it.

The ratio-based channel comparison is robust experimental design: fixed W/LYSO stack, same beam, only the light-collection channel swapped — the 2.2x light-per-GeV and 3.5x response-per-MIP DSB1/LuAG ratios are genuine, transferable measurements even with a soft absolute scale (index.html Materials table + units caveat).

Exemplary systematics forensics on the energy response: the apparent high-E saturation was prosecuted through four hypotheses (transverse leakage acquitted, SiPM pixel saturation acquitted, MIP gain-monitoring struck down as species- and estimator-biased, Longo shower-max migration convicted in part) — FINDINGS.md lines 468-497. The team demonstrably understands its own energy systematics, including invalidating its own calibration anchor.

The one intrinsic statement that exists was obtained correctly: erfc fit to the direct-hit edge giving sigma/E <= 10.5 ± 1.6% at 5 GeV, with its residual contamination (position falloff, momentum bite) stated plainly (FINDINGS.md lines 102-110).

Correct self-diagnosis of the blocking systematic: the log explicitly identifies the beam-spot/position degeneracy as the limit and impact-position tagging as the fix, with statistics ruled out as the remedy (lines 106-110, 123-127) — the required next measurement is already in their own plan, including the gain-monitor fix list (temperature logging + pulser + muon-stopper MIP anchor, line ~492-497).

Mean-response physics behaves as the fixed-depth-sampling model predicts: linear above 3 GeV, sub-linear below (line 322-323), high-E residuals consistent with linear x Longo once the gain ladder is accounted — the concept is at least self-consistent at the mean level.

The timing result that anchors the alternative framing is strong and carefully error-budgeted: reference jitter independently validated at 107-114 ps via the diagonal-difference estimator, and the estimator's own failure mode on the high-light channel (correlated capillary terms) was caught rather than published as a false intrinsic number.
weaknesses: CRITICAL — No intrinsic energy resolution was measured at any scan point. Every quoted sigma/E (33.6% at 5 GeV, 20.4% at 7, 31.9% at 9 — FINDINGS.md lines 227, 340, 362) is position-smearing dominated; the sole intrinsic statement is a single upper bound at a single energy (<=10.5 ± 1.6% at 5 GeV) with zero discrimination power between a 3%/sqrt(E) and a 20%/sqrt(E) device. For an energy-measurement case there is, strictly, no measurement.

CRITICAL — Linearity is established only to a ±15% cross-run gain envelope with no gain monitor, and the dataset cannot be tightened retroactively (MIP normalization proven invalid, lines 481-483). FCC-ee EM physics requires scale control roughly two orders of magnitude better; the campaign is not merely short of the goal, it has no path to it from existing data.

MAJOR — Maximum energy 11 GeV (and that point open-markered for halo purity), i.e. one quarter of the FCC-ee Z-pole electron energy; the constant-term-dominated regime that decides FCC-ee viability is completely unexplored.

MAJOR — Dynamic range already fails at 11 GeV: the LG ceiling (~13.6k ADC-eq) compresses DSB1's contained peak (8.0 GeV-equivalent vs 9.7 for LuAG in the 11 GeV trial; FINDINGS.md '11 GeV reinterpretation' and line 565-567). The better light channel outruns the readout at 1/4 of target energy — the readout architecture for FCC-ee/muon-collider energies is undemonstrated.

MAJOR — Single 14x14 mm module, no surrounding matrix: miss fractions 8-54% across the scan, lateral containment never measured absolutely (only acquitted as the saturation cause at the ±3% level), no shower sharing, no cluster-level or particle-flow-relevant performance.

MAJOR — The concept-defining number for a shower-max sampler used as an energy device — the event-by-event longitudinal depth-fluctuation contribution to sigma/E — was neither measured nor bounded. The Longo migration correction (-3.2/-6.0/-8.5% at 7/9/11 GeV) corrects the mean response only; whether shower-max stationarity actually keeps depth fluctuations second-order in this geometry's longitudinal acceptance is the make-or-break question and it is open.

MAJOR — No absolute energy scale: ADC-eq is readout-relative, no photoelectron calibration yet (dark-pulse method 'possible and planned'), so no photostatistics-term prediction against which a future resolution measurement can be decomposed.

MAJOR — No hadronic response measured and e/pi separation quantified only at one tag-and-probe training point (90.9%/x3, or 73.4%/x19 with energy window — lines 302-305); no rejection-vs-energy curve, no lead-converter control runs taken (they were requested in the log but not executed).

MAJOR (for 'does it matter') — Radiation hardness, the concept's stated motivation for shower-max capillary readout, was not measured this campaign; the muon-collider case in particular rests on it entirely.

MINOR — 1 GeV energy point compromised (peak merges with the miss ridge, line 323-325); 11 GeV halo/miss class unexplained (LuAG 467 miss vs 187 contained); run 34 pion-contaminated and run 36 mixed-config — all already documented, none load-bearing for the energy verdict.
open_questions: What is the event-by-event longitudinal-fluctuation term of fixed-depth sampling in this geometry? Quantify the second derivative of the Longo-weighted response around shower max for the capillary window's effective longitudinal acceptance (in X0), via simulation validated against the measured -3 to -8.5% mean migration — is the term <=1-2% or does it dominate?
What is the absolute photoelectron yield per GeV (dark-pulse calibration, planned but not done), and does the implied photostatistics term support anything better than ~10%/sqrt(E)?

Does the correlated-capillary effect discovered in DSB1 timing (shared shower fluctuations defeating the diagonal estimator) have an energy-side analogue — a correlated floor in the 4-capillary sum resolution that averaging cannot remove?
How much of the 10.5 ± 1.6% bound at 5 GeV is T10 momentum bite and position falloff, i.e. how far does the bound actually drop with a tracker? (A re-run with impact tagging answers this directly.)
What is the true lateral containment fraction of one 14x14 mm cell against the W/LYSO effective Moliere radius, and what does a 3x3 matrix recover — both for resolution and for position-from-sharing?
Can the dual-gain readout be rescoped to 45-100 GeV showers (LG ceiling fix) while preserving MIP-scale overlap for calibration?

Does the DSB:Ce light-collection advantage (2.2x) and the 79 ps constant term survive realistic FCC-ee / muon-collider integrated doses — the radiation-hardness campaign that motivates the whole architecture?
What is e/pi rejection vs energy at fixed electron efficiency, measured with the lead-converter control runs the log already requested (FINDINGS.md lines ~305-309)?

Is the ~75 ps ref-subtracted DSB1 point at 9 GeV real (downstream reference, 'rich man's estimator', planned next beam test)? This decides whether the timing-layer framing extrapolates to few-tens-of-ps at Z-pole energies.

For the FCC-ee pitch specifically: is the target to BE the EM calorimeter (then the full sigma/E program below is mandatory) or to be a timing/position/preshower layer embedded in a crystal or SiW calorimeter (then energy linearity per-cell and rad hardness matter, but the stochastic-term race does not)? The collaboration should choose before the next test beam, because the two answers order the measurement program differently.
recommendation: CONDITIONAL PROCEED, WITH REFRAMING. Judge and fund this as what the data show: a demonstrated hundred-picosecond timing (plus coarse position) layer at shower max in a radiation-hard-by-design light-collection architecture, with an OPEN, undemonstrated calorimeter case. Do not allow the word 'calorimeter' in a performance sense in proposals until the following gate is passed. Required measurement program, in priority order: (1) PS re-run with impact-position tagging (tracker or mm-scale hodoscope/collimation), per-run gain monitoring (temperature log + LED/pulser + species-pure stopper-muon MIP anchor — all already in the team's own fix list, FINDINGS.md ~line 492), and the absolute pe/GeV dark-pulse calibration: deliverable = intrinsic sigma/E at 1-9 GeV decomposed into photostatistics + sampling + constant terms, and linearity to the percent level. (2) SPS run (H2/H4, 10-100 GeV) with rescoped LG dynamic range and a 3x3 module matrix: deliverable = stochastic and constant terms in the FCC-ee-relevant regime, lateral containment/sharing, e/pi rejection vs E with converter control runs, plus the downstream time reference to confirm the ~75 ps intrinsic timing point. (3) Parallel irradiation campaign on DSB:Ce and LuAG:Ce capillaries with before/after light-yield AND timing-constant-term measurements — without this the muon-collider pitch has no evidentiary basis. DECISION GATE for the calorimeter claim: intrinsic sigma/E <= ~10%/sqrt(E) with constant term <= ~1-2% and percent-level linearity demonstrated to >=50 GeV. If passed, the concept is a rare both-at-once device (energy + tens-of-ps timing) and genuinely interesting for FCC-ee particle flow and muon-collider BIB rejection. If failed, the fallback is still valuable and fundable: an embedded shower-max timing/position layer — but that competes against dedicated timing layers (LGAD/crystal-bar designs) on ps-per-dollar and rad hardness, not on energy resolution, and the proposal should be costed accordingly. On the evidence as published (index.html), the team's own claims are consistent with this framing; the panel risk is not overclaiming by the proponents but over-reading by reviewers — the synthesis should state explicitly that intrinsic energy resolution remains unmeasured.
